clue.text: Have nothing to do with row surrounding broadcast

indicators.note: surrounding tells us the word for a row is placed around the word for broadcast

parts.note: a row is a racket or noise, a din
to broadcast seed is to sow it

explanation.surface: Someone cuts ties after a quarrel over something put on air.
explanation.definitionFit: To renounce or refuse to acknowledge something is to cut all connection with it.

clue.text: Location device went off round church after being set up

indicators.note: in a down clue, being set up means the assembled letters are read upwards, back to front
round says the word for went off is wrapped around the church abbreviation

parts.note: food that went off has rotted
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A tracking gadget malfunctioned near a church once it had been installed.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'set up' reads upwards, so the reversal applies to the whole container after 'round' has put the church inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal or signal finder is an instrument used to locate hidden things.

clue.text: Society needs nerve to oust a pest

indicators.note: to oust means to throw out, so the letter named next is removed from the word for nerve

parts.note: nerve in the sense of bravery is courage

explanation.surface: A community must find the courage to get rid of a pest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to oust' removes A from COURAGE, leaving COURGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plague or persistent affliction is something that torments, as a pest does.

clue.text: Shrewd over opening for

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Shrewd over opening for (9)': cut short after 'for', so the definition (a joke) is missing; WISE over CRACK gives the wordplay but no search found the full clue.

clue.text: Sweet courses unfinished before a drop of brandy?

indicators.note: unfinished means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a syllabus sets out the courses of study

indicators.note: a drop of brandy is just a tiny bit of it, its opening letter

explanation.surface: A dessert comes after an incomplete set of courses, with a splash of brandy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts SYLLABUS to SYLLABU. A syllabub is an old English pudding of whipped cream with wine or brandy.
explanation.definitionFit: A creamy whipped pudding is a dessert, which the British call a sweet.

clue.text: I quite agree I'm under instruction

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of emphatic agreement with what someone has just said
read literally, someone is informing or instructing the speaker

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom of strong agreement, and literally describes someone being informed by another person.

clue.text: Horse writer almost upset Sussex town

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the letters upside down, so they read upwards
almost says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Anna Sewell wrote Black Beauty, the story of a horse

explanation.surface: A novelist about horses is nearly distraught in a Sussex town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts SEWELL to SEWEL; 'upset' reverses it. Lewes is the county town of East Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewes is a historic town in southern England, the administrative centre of East Sussex.

clue.text: Worst one — a gangster?- is cruel

parts.note: to worst someone is to defeat them, to best them
the Roman numeral I is one
Al Capone was the famous Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: The worst person of all, a mobster perhaps, is brutal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worst' looks like an adjective but is the verb meaning to beat, BEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Savage, animal-like behaviour is brutal and merciless.

clue.text: I supply drink in British jug

parts.note: British gives BR
a ewer is a large water jug

explanation.surface: A drinks maker speaks from inside a British jug.
explanation.definitionFit: A maker of beer provides people with drink, so the first person describes that trade.

clue.text: Granted, some go crazy about college, requiring further loan

indicators.note: about puts the scrambled letters around the abbreviation for college
crazy says the letters of these words are scrambled

explanation.surface: Admittedly, some students go wild at university and need more money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' rearranges GRANTED SOME GO, and 'about' wraps that round C.
explanation.definitionFit: A further borrowing secured against a house already mortgaged is an additional loan.

clue.text: Clothes for a honeymoon start to titillate and arouse us cheekily

indicators.note: start to picks out the first letter of the word that follows
cheekily suggests the letters behave impudently and are shuffled

explanation.surface: A bride packs racy outfits for the wedding trip to excite her new husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheekily' is the anagram signal, sitting at the end so the clue reads as a saucy suggestion; 'start to' gives the T.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride's collection of clothes and linen, traditionally assembled for marriage and the wedding trip.

clue.text: Desert and what it lacks mostly, being filled by sun

indicators.note: being filled by says the next letter goes inside the shortened word
mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: a desert lacks water

explanation.surface: An arid region lacks rain but is flooded with sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims WATER to WATE, and 'being filled by' puts S inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A barren wilderness is an empty wasteland.

clue.text: Drink from scoundrel, one about to get a round

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible man
A means one
C stands for circa, about
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A villain orders a drink and then gets a round in.
explanation.walkthrough: Curacao is an orange-flavoured liqueur from the Caribbean island of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: An orange liqueur is an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Follow to receive computer equipment with facilities attached (2,5) 141 taken in by some gag

indicators.note: to receive says the word for follow takes the letters for computer equipment inside

parts.note: to follow on is to ensue
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: A hotel room follows on, with computer kit and its own bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: The feed adds stray words from the next clue after the count; the clue proper ends at 'attached'.
explanation.definitionFit: A room with its own bathroom connected is described this way.

clue.text: I'm the last character to be taken in by some gag

indicators.note: taken in by says the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A comic admits to being fooled by a joke, ending up last.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'sOME GAg'.
explanation.definitionFit: The final letter of the Greek alphabet speaks for itself.

clue.text: Confused 'mile 'and 'yard' in a haze

indicators.note: confused says the letters of the two quoted words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone muddles up imperial units of distance in a daze.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something vaguely as if half asleep is acting in a haze.

clue.text: Heart's given to former lover in this county

parts.note: the heart is the middle, and the 's is kept as an S
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: An old flame wins someone's heart in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Middlesex is a former English county now largely absorbed into London.
explanation.definitionFit: Middlesex is a historic shire of England.

clue.text: Port suitable for abbot, it appears

definitions.text: Port suitable for abbot, it appears

parts.words: Port suitable for abbot, it appears
parts.note: the harbour town's name, split in two, reads as a description of a religious leader such as an abbot

explanation.surface: A harbour that seems tailor-made for a monastery's chief.
explanation.walkthrough: The Welsh ferry port on Anglesey splits into two words describing the pious leader of a monastery.
explanation.definitionFit: A ferry town in north Wales is a harbour, and an abbot is a pious head of a religious house.

clue.text: Support canoe manoeuvre beside side of river

indicators.note: beside puts the canoe move next to the river's edge, after it in the answer

parts.note: a river's side is its bank
a roll is the canoeist's move of turning over and back up

explanation.surface: A paddler practises a capsize drill next to the riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: To bankroll is to fund or finance, giving financial backing.

clue.text: I'm tucking into beers and spirits ultimately without end

indicators.note: tucking into says I'M goes inside the word for beers

parts.note: ales are beers

indicators.note: ultimately picks the last letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A drinker gets stuck into beer and spirits with no particular goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without end' is the definition, not a deletion signal: aimless means lacking an end in view.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking a goal or purpose means acting without an end in view.

clue.text: Director is leading company dance

indicators.note: leading means the previous letters go in front of the next piece

explanation.surface: A director heads a company of dancers.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a party or club evening for dancing to recorded pop music.

clue.text: Fan's view of own goal, perhaps, from team containing United, I see

definitions.text: Fan's view of own goal, perhaps

indicators.note: containing says the team word holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: a side is a team
U is the usual abbreviation for United in team names
C sounds like see, used as a letter

explanation.surface: A supporter watches their United team concede to itself, groaning.
explanation.walkthrough: A supporter might call an own goal suicide. 'see' gives C, the letter that is said the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: Fans call scoring into one's own net self-destruction, a figurative killing of oneself.

clue.text: Escaping f-falsity

parts.note: the stammered opening gives a lone F
falsity is lying

explanation.surface: A stammering fugitive tells lies on the run.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammer gives F before the synonym for falsity.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleeing or escaping can be described as flying, as in flying from danger.

clue.text: Composer and lecturer with skill, receiving honour

indicators.note: receiving says the word for skill takes the honour inside it

parts.note: art is skill
an MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A musician and an academic with talent get an award.
explanation.walkthrough: Constant Lambert was an English composer and conductor of the 20th century.
explanation.definitionFit: Constant Lambert wrote music such as The Rio Grande.

clue.text: Additional component of sex trade

indicators.note: component of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A side issue within the sex industry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something supplementary is more than the usual amount.

clue.text: Nothing in policy till unequivocally backed

indicators.note: backed says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Nothing in the policy was supported without reservation until now.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run backwards across 'policY TILL UNequivocally'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something legally void or without substance amounts to nothing.

clue.text: That is a chap in it

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: taken as written
Des is a man's name, short for Desmond

explanation.surface: A man is identified as being right there in the thick of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Id est is Latin for 'that is', abbreviated i.e.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase translates as 'that is', used to clarify.

clue.text: Member is almost bound to accept combatants' first truce

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body

indicators.note: to accept says the shortened word takes a letter inside
almost says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: bound means tied

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A soldier is nearly obliged to take up the fighters' first ceasefire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts TIED to TIE, and 'to accept' puts C (first of 'combatants'') inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An armistice is an agreement to stop fighting, a ceasefire.

clue.text: Thin energetic person latches on to return of service

indicators.note: latches on to says the energetic person grabs hold of the reversed piece, wrapping round it

parts.note: a goer is an energetic, lively person

indicators.note: return of says the letters of the next word come back reversed

parts.note: Mass is a church service

explanation.surface: A lively player seizes on the opponent's serve to hit it back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of service' sounds like tennis; here service is a church Mass, read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossamer describes something very fine and delicate, flimsy like cobwebs.

clue.text: No time for writing before completion? Ease deadline

indicators.note: before puts the first piece in front of the next
no time means the abbreviation for time is taken away

parts.note: text is writing
the end is completion

explanation.surface: A writer short of time asks to be let off the due date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' removes a T from TEXT, leaving EXT.
explanation.definitionFit: To lengthen the time allowed is to push back a deadline.
